section_summary: This section comprises an English translation of Chapters VI through IX of an educational textbook on democracy prepared for postwar Japan. It examines the nature of public opinion and methods of propaganda necessary for an enlightened electorate, citizen participation in local and national governance, and the role and abuses of political parties. It further contrasts democratic individualism and social ethics with feudalism and totalitarianism, concluding with an introduction to economic democracy and the evolution of free-enterprise capitalism.

subfiles.about: An English translation of chapters from a Japanese civic textbook explaining the principles of democracy, public opinion, governance, political parties, social ethics, and economic life.
subfiles.summary: This instructional text educates postwar Japanese citizens on the foundational principles of democratic society, opening with guidance on how to evaluate propaganda critically and foster an enlightened electorate. It emphasizes individual civic responsibility, detailing local autonomy, national parliamentary governance, and both the function and abuses of competitive political parties. The text contrasts democratic individualism, human dignity, and horizontal social ethics against feudal traditions and totalitarian regimes. Finally, it outlines democracy in economic life, discussing the origins, benefits, and need for public welfare regulation within free-market capitalism.
subfiles.title: Primer of Democracy (Chapters VI-IX)
